title: Anthropic Removes Daily Usage Limits
content:
Anthropic just removed one of Claude’s biggest usage limits — but not for everyone
Claude Code users on Anthropic’s $200 plan will no longer face a rolling five-hour usage cap, provided their accounts are verified and they have weekly usage left.
Anthropic announced the change Friday as it renamed its two top consumer plans. Max 5x is now Max, and Max 20x becomes Ultra. They still cost $100 and $200 a month, respectively, and current subscribers don’t need to do anything to switch.
Max 5x is now Max, and Max 20x becomes Ultra.
Anthropic’s pricing page also lists monthly Claude Platform API credits: $100 with Max and $200 with Ultra. That adds another consideration for developers who use Claude Code while building applications against the API, with each plan bundling API credits equal to its monthly subscription price. Claude Code creator Boris Cherny highlighted the limit change in his own post.
What the five-hour cap meant
The five-hour limit capped usage within a rolling window, and a demanding task could burn through that allowance much sooner. Claude Code users could hit it midway through debugging or a large refactor and have to wait for a reset despite having weekly usage left.
Verification comes first
Some Ultra subscribers will have to wait for Anthropic to verify their accounts before the five-hour limit goes away. The company says the checks help prevent fraud and abuse, and it will email users when the cap is lifted.
Some Ultra subscribers will have to wait for Anthropic to verify their accounts before the five-hour limit goes away.
According to Anthropic’, verification happens automatically based on account and payment history. There’s no way to request it or speed it up so some users will just have to be patient.
The weekly cap remains
Ultra users still have the same weekly allowance, and they could use it up sooner without the five-hour limit forcing them to pause. The pricing page lists Ultra at 10 times Pro’s weekly usage, compared with five times Pro’s weekly usage on Max.
The pricing page lists Ultra at 10 times Pro’s weekly usage, compared with five times Pro’s weekly usage on Max.
Your chats with Claude count toward the same weekly limit as your Claude Code sessions, whether you’re on the web, desktop, or mobile. Once you use up that allowance, you can turn on usage credits to keep working at standard API rates, though you’ll pay extra on top of your subscription.
If you keep hitting the session limit with weekly usage to spare, avoiding those interruptions could make Ultra worth the extra $100 a month over Max, but if you already run out before the week is over, removing the session cap won’t give you more included usage.
OpenAI eases its limits
A day earlier, OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux announced higher usage limits for Pro subscribers and Business Premium.
OpenAI also dropped a planned cut for existing $200 Pro subscribers after customers objected. In a separate pricing decision, the company abandoned an idea to replace token-based billing with flat per-job fees after developers pushed back.
Learning Path

report.summary: Anthropic renamed its top tiers to Max and Ultra and scrapped the rolling five-hour Claude Code session cap for verified $200 Ultra subscribers, while keeping weekly limits intact.
report.background: Agentic coding tools such as Claude Code can burn enormous amounts of inference in a single long debugging or refactoring session, so vendors impose layered rate limits to control GPU costs. Anthropic's structure has been a rolling five-hour window sitting on top of a weekly allowance. The five-hour cap was widely criticized because a heavy task could exhaust it in under an hour, forcing power users to pause mid-work even with weekly quota left. Meanwhile competition for high-spending developers has intensified: OpenAI, Google, and Cursor all court the same $100–$200/month power-user segment, and rate limits have become a visible differentiator. Anthropic's change — paired with a renaming of its two Max tiers and bundled API credits — reframes the top plans around developers running agents rather than casual chat users.
key_points: Max 5x is now simply Max at $100/month, and Max 20x becomes Ultra at $200/month. Existing subscribers are migrated automatically with no action required. Both plans now bundle monthly Claude Platform API credits equal to their subscription price — $100 and $200 respectively — which matters for developers building apps against the API while using Claude Code.

The removed limit was a rolling five-hour usage window that throttled Claude Code users mid-task, even when they still had weekly allowance remaining. Heavy debugging sessions or large refactors could exhaust the window quickly and force a wait for reset. Removing it means Ultra users no longer hit unpredictable hard stops during long uninterrupted work.

The change is gated behind account verification. Some Ultra subscribers must wait for Anthropic to verify their account details and payment history before the session cap lifts. Verification is automatic — there is no request form and no way to speed it up. Anthropic says the checks exist to prevent fraud and abuse, and will email users when the cap is removed.

The weekly cap is untouched and remains the binding constraint. Ultra includes 10x Pro's weekly usage; Max includes 5x. Critically, ordinary Claude chats on web, desktop, and mobile count against the same weekly pool as Claude Code sessions. Once exhausted, users can enable usage credits and keep working at standard API rates, paying on top of the subscription.

Anthropic moved a day after OpenAI raised limits for Pro and Business Premium subscribers. OpenAI also reversed a planned cut for existing $200 Pro subscribers after customer complaints, and abandoned a proposal to replace token-based billing with flat per-job fees following developer pushback — evidence that vendor pricing and limit decisions are now highly sensitive to user reaction.

The practical read is that the $100 Max-to-$200 Ultra upgrade buys fewer interruptions, not more total included usage. If you routinely exhaust your weekly allowance before the week ends, dropping the session cap will not help you. It only helps users who repeatedly stall at the five-hour wall with weekly quota to spare.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is a signal that rate limits have become a competitive lever rather than a back-office detail: two leading labs adjusted top-tier allowances within 24 hours of each other, and both backed off from unpopular restrictions. For developers, the immediate benefit is predictability — long agentic runs, big refactors, and multi-hour debugging no longer get interrupted by an opaque five-hour wall. But the weekly ceiling becomes the real budget, so teams will need to plan usage across chat and coding sessions, and heavier users may end up paying metered API rates regardless. For regular users, almost nothing changes: the free and Pro tiers are untouched, and the change only affects a small population of $200/month subscribers. The broader effect is a gradual blurring of consumer subscription and developer platform pricing.
report.tools: To follow this shift, watch Claude Code itself and Anthropic's pricing page for the Ultra verification rollout. Open-source usage trackers like ccusage let Claude Code users monitor token burn and weekly remaining quota. LiteLLM provides a proxy for routing and metering across providers if you want to compare Claude Code against OpenAI's Codex CLI or Gemini CLI. Aider and Cline are strong open-source agentic coding alternatives worth benchmarking on cost per task before committing to a $200 tier.
